PullRequest.Title: Add opt-in auto-archive inactive sessions with merged pull requests
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- add two disabled-by-default, application-scoped Preview settings:
  - `chat.agentSessions.autoArchiveMergedSessionsAfterDays` controls inactivity before automatic archival
  - `chat.agentSessions.autoDeleteArchivedMergedSessionsAfterDays` controls the grace period after automatic archival before permanent deletion
- allow either lifecycle stage to be enabled or disabled independently with 1, 7, 15, or 30 day thresholds
- archive inactive agent sessions only after their designated pull request is authoritatively confirmed merged
- permanently delete only sessions carrying durable automatic-archive provenance after the independently configured deletion grace period
- expose independent enterprise policies:
  - `ChatAgentSessionsAutoArchiveMergedSessionsAfterDays`
  - `ChatAgentSessionsAutoDeleteArchivedMergedSessionsAfterDays`
- synchronize both settings into Agent Host root configuration and keep startup/hourly candidate evaluation authoritative in the host
- prefilter archived deletion candidates from durable metadata before restoring sessions
- refresh pull request state before each action and revalidate the relevant setting, session state, retention period, and designated pull request inside the deletion critical section
- preserve manually archived sessions, clear automatic-archive provenance on unarchive, and retain sessions whose archived worktree still exists
- use the existing archive and deletion lifecycle paths so persistence, provider callbacks, registry updates, client updates, and safe worktree cleanup remain consistent
- keep the one-time opt-in notification in the workbench as UI only; enabling it sets both thresholds to 15 days

## Demo

No visual capture: the only new UI is a standard VS Code notification and two Settings enums. When both cleanup settings are disabled, an inactive merged-PR session offers **Turn On Session Cleanup** and **Open Settings**. Enabling cleanup archives eligible sessions after 15 days of inactivity and permanently deletes them 15 days later.

## Safety

- permanent deletion applies only when a durable automatic-archive timestamp establishes the full configured deletion grace period; manually archived and pre-existing archived sessions are not deleted
- unarchiving clears the automatic-archive timestamp for both loaded and unloaded sessions, so a later manual re-archive cannot inherit deletion eligibility
- disabling or changing the relevant setting, reopening the pull request, or unarchiving the session aborts the corresponding lifecycle action during final validation
- unarchive actions are rejected once deletion has entered its critical section, preventing session/worktree restoration from racing destructive cleanup
- automatic deletion fails closed while an archived worktree remains or its state cannot be inspected

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- targeted Agent Host lifecycle, passive-unarchive, and policy tests — 40 passing
- targeted GitHub contribution browser tests — 16 passing
- targeted ESLint for all changed TypeScript files
- `npm run export-policy-data`
- `git diff --check`
- `npm run typecheck-client` reports no errors in changed files; the branch retains unrelated `@github/copilot-sdk` type failures

Fixes #334334
Fixes #334352

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed ordering, hourly retry, and expensive restore call path are explicit. Only the prevalence of retained worktrees is uncertain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: GitHub API calls, provider/session database reads, transcript objects, and provider chat materialization/release work.
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Once per hourly pass for each retained-worktree session past the deletion cutoff; restore cost also grows with transcript and chat metadata size.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Persistent background network/filesystem I/O and CPU/GC pressure.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: There was no background deletion pass restoring archived sessions before this PR.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new hourly lifecycle restores every due deletion candidate before checking whether its retained worktree makes automatic deletion impossible; rejected candidates remain eligible and repeat the sequence next hour.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 144 unconditionally awaits `_accessor.restoreSession(session)` before the delete branch reaches the added `canDeleteSession` worktree guard at lines 188-191.
Findings.Title: Preflight retained worktrees before restoring deletion candidates
Findings.Impact: Automatically archived sessions whose worktree cleanup was skipped or failed repeatedly consume GitHub API budget and provider/database I/O every hour despite being unable to make deletion progress.
Findings.Evidence: `restoreSession` materializes the provider chat, loads message history, and hydrates metadata/configuration. The later worktree guard only reads persisted worktree metadata and performs `fs.access`, so it can reject without restored session state. A rejected deletion keeps its archive timestamp and is returned by the next hourly candidate scan.
Findings.Recommendation: For delete candidates, run a cheap `canDeleteSession` preflight before the GitHub refresh and restore, while retaining the current in-disposal recheck for race safety.

Scenarios.Scenario: Startup and hourly auto-archive of inactive sessions whose designated pull request has merged
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The lifecycle starts asynchronously when a provider is available and is not on the editor startup critical path. Within the cleanup pass, registry enumeration and candidate metadata reads must complete before candidates are processed; each candidate then waits for an authoritative GitHub refresh and, when merged, a full session restore before archive dispatch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One registry query per enabled lifecycle pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Gates candidate enumeration, but only on the background lifecycle pass.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open per-session databases and read archive/provenance/GitHub metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one metadata read for each registry entry that survives in-memory/time filtering, with concurrency 4.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No hourly lifecycle metadata sweep occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Gates construction of the background candidate list.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authoritatively fetch the designated pull request core state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequential refresh per effective candidate; authoritative refreshes bypass warm snapshot reuse.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only client-watched sessions had PR status subscriptions; no lifecycle refresh occurred.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Gates each candidate action, but not interactive startup.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Materialize the provider chat, load transcript/messages, hydrate metadata/config/customizations, and restore host state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once for each cold candidate authoritatively reported merged; warm restored sessions short-circuit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Cold sessions were restored only when another consumer requested them, not by an hourly cleanup pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Gates archive dispatch for that candidate and serializes progress to later candidates.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Inspect/commit/remove a session worktree through git-backed worktree cleanup.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one branch/status/commit/remove sequence per successfully archived worktree session; operations for different sessions may overlap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same cleanup already ran for manual archive; the diff newly reaches it from automatic archive.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Fire-and-forget after archive dispatch, so it does not gate the lifecycle loop but can create background subprocess overlap.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of internal inactive registry sessions after time/status filtering; effective network/restore cardinality is the number with designated PR metadata, and successful archive work scales with those authoritatively merged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Registry metadata inspection is limited to 4. Candidate evaluation is serialized by the `for`/`await` loop. Worktree cleanup and provider archive callbacks are launched asynchronously per session and can overlap across sessions because sequencing is keyed by session ID.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Live summaries avoid some database reads. Cold sessions require metadata reads. Pull-request resources retain dormant snapshots briefly, but lifecycle requests are authoritative and therefore fetch. Restored sessions are warm only while resident; archived residency is eligible for release.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all boundary placement, cardinality controls, and serialization are explicit in the changed code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large catalog sizes and provider restore durations vary, but the pass is opt-in, hourly, and off the interactive critical path.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: the general one-time archive work is deliberately background, metadata reads are limited, and candidate processing avoids a concurrency burst.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hourly permanent-deletion evaluation for automatically archived sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Candidate metadata enumeration, authoritative PR refresh, and full session restore all complete before conditional deletion validation. The worktree existence check then gates destructive disposal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read archive provenance and GitHub metadata from each candidate session database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One bounded-concurrency metadata read per potentially archived internal session during each enabled pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No automatic deletion candidate scan existed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Authoritatively refresh pull request core state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequential request per due deletion candidate on every pass, including candidates later blocked by a worktree.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Archived sessions were not refreshed hourly for deletion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore provider chat/session state and transcript.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per cold due deletion candidate per pass; for retained-worktree candidates it can recur hourly after archived residency is released.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No background restore of archived sessions for deletion existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Gates the later worktree eligibility check and deletion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read worktree metadata and test worktree path existence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One check per due candidate, but only after network refresh and restore.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Rejects deletion when the worktree remains.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Tombstone the registry entry and delete per-session persisted data after final validation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per candidate that passes every validation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same disposal path ran only for explicit deletion; the diff invokes it automatically.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of automatically archived sessions past the grace period. The reported repeated cost is specifically the effective subset whose worktree still exists, multiplied by every hourly pass and by transcript size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Candidates are processed one at a time. Metadata prefiltering uses concurrency 4. Disposal is guarded per session; archived residency reconciliation runs asynchronously afterward.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Archive provenance remains eligible after worktree rejection. Restored archived sessions are eligible for residency release, so the next pass can be cold again. No negative cache or early worktree prefilter suppresses retries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the restore-before-guard ordering and unchanged hourly eligibility are explicit, and the guard does not require restored state.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of retained worktrees depends on branch/worktree cleanup outcomes, but missing branches, cleanup failures, or unreleasable worktrees are explicit supported states.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported: retained-worktree candidates repeatedly incur network and full restoration work before an inexpensive guard rejects deletion.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench prompt for opting into merged-session cleanup
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The prompt autorun executes when the already-polled designated PR model, archive state, session status, update time, or cleanup setting changes. It is UI-only and does not gate session operations.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Poll pull request, CI, and review-thread models.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing polling cardinality remains one model set per tracked PR; the added prompt observes the existing designated PR model.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same PR polling occurred before the prompt observer was added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The prompt waits for existing PR data but adds no network request.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/store the one-time application prompt marker and update two user settings when accepted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Storage read when an eligible autorun fires; one marker write and two configuration writes when the prompt is first shown/accepted.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No cleanup prompt or setting writes existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Small synchronous/application configuration work on a rare UI transition.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Tracked unarchived PR sessions, but only the first designated PR per session receives the prompt autorun and the prompt marker suppresses repeated UI.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One autorun is attached to the designated PR poller for each tracked unarchived session; application storage ensures only one prompt is shown.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing PR model/resource caching is reused. The durable prompted flag is the negative cache for future prompts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Session count varies, but added observer work is small and does not add polling.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the new observer reuses existing polling and durable prompt suppression prevents repeated user-visible work.

Scenarios.CriticalPath: Unarchive persists the normal archived flag and now clears automatic-archive provenance; configuration changes propagate the two numeric settings to the host and schedule a background pass.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist archived-state and clear automatic-archive timestamp in the session database.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two small metadata writes per loaded-session unarchive; unloaded handling batches values in one call.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Unarchive wrote only the archived flag.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Rare action-side persistence, not a scaling hot path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Propagate application configuration to Agent Host and schedule cleanup evaluation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One coalesced scheduled run when either effective threshold changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No cleanup settings or scheduled evaluation existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background and serialized; disabled thresholds return before registry I/O.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Individual unarchive operations and infrequent setting changes, not collection size.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The two unarchive metadata writes use existing persistence helpers; configuration-triggered lifecycle runs are coalesced by `RunOnceScheduler` and serialized by `_runPromise`.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Threshold values are cached in the lifecycle object and unchanged root-config events are ignored.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: added persistence is bounded to a rare action, and scheduling is coalesced/serialized.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 26 changed files and the complete new lifecycle test diff. One performance regression was reported: deletion candidates blocked by retained worktrees repeatedly pay authoritative network refresh and full session restoration before the worktree guard rejects them. Other added work is opt-in/background, bounded or coalesced, and did not meet the threshold for another performance finding.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
